question: Which special order of the courts means “arrested person should be presented before the court"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Habeas corpus**__.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **special order of the courts, Habeas corpus**, means **“arrested person should be presented before the court"**.
 
• **Habeas corpus** is a legal remedy that **allows a person to inform a court about an illegitimate arrest or imprisonment** and ask that the court compel the person's custodian—typically a prison official—to bring the prisoner to court so that the validity of the arrest can be determined.
 
• **William Blackstone **referred to the **writ of habeas corpus** as a** "great and efficient writ in all manner of illrgal confinement"**.
 
• **Habeas corpus** is a summons that has the** same legal effect as a court order**; it is** directed to the custodian and requests that a prisoner be brought before the court together with documentation of the custodian's authority** so that the court can evaluate if the custodian has the right to hold the prisoner

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• .A **judicial remedy **known as a **mandamus** is an** order from a court to any government, subordinate court, corporation, or public authority** directing them to perform (or refrain from performing) a particular act that they are legally required to perform (or refrain from performing), and which is in the nature of a public duty and, in some cases, a **statutory duty**.
 
• **Certiorari** is a legal procedure **used to ask for judicial review of a ruling made by a lower court or government** **body**.
 
• A writ of prerogative known as a **quo warranto demands that the person to whom it is addressed provide proof of their legal capacity** to exercise a right, power, or franchise.
